The implementation plan and its design artifacts are ready. **This is the plan-review gate — please review before I generate tasks or write any code.**

## 📐 Plan ready — `specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md`

**Artifacts:** `plan.md`, `research.md` (12 decisions), `data-model.md`, `contracts/` (api, search-grammar, netscape-format), `quickstart.md`. Constitution file is an unfilled template, so there are no ratified project gates; I held the plan to the method's baseline (spec-first, simplicity, testability) — it passes with no complexity to justify.

### The core architectural decision — why there's a server

Three features you approved **can't** be done by a browser alone, because browsers block cross-origin reads of other sites (CORS):
- **auto-metadata** (fetch the page's title/description/favicon/preview),
- **self-contained HTML snapshots** (fetch the page + all its resources),
- **Internet Archive saving** (cross-origin POST to archive.org).

So the app is **one local Node process** that serves the UI *and* a small API on port 4000, with all data stored **on your device**. "Same-device storage" is preserved — the server and its database live on the same machine you run the app on.

### Proposed stack

| Layer | Choice | Why |
|-------|--------|-----|
| Server | **Node.js 24 + Express** | Provided by the runtime; serves UI + API on `0.0.0.0:4000` via `npm start` |
| Storage | **SQLite (better-sqlite3)** + filesystem for snapshots/images | Single-user, same-device, no separate service; handles 500+ easily |
| UI | **React + Vite** (built, served by the server) | Rich interactions: live search, bulk select, tag-suggest, Markdown preview |
| Metadata | server fetch + **cheerio**; async (`pending`→`complete/failed`) | Non-blocking saves |
| Snapshots | **Playwright 1.61.0 / Chromium** (already installed) → self-contained HTML; PDFs passed through | Reuses the pinned browser; no second download |
| Notes | **marked + DOMPurify** | Safe Markdown rendering |
| Search | hand-written tokenizer + parser | Needed for `#tag`+boolean+phrase+literal-when-quoted rules |
| Tests | **node:test** (unit) + **Playwright** (E2E) | Cover risky logic + journeys |

### What the design artifacts pin down

- **data-model.md** — tables for bookmark, tag (unique `name_key` enforcing your single-identity rule FR-008a), bookmark_tags join, saved_search (include/exclude tags), snapshot (html/pdf), preferences singleton; plus state transitions (metadata, archive⇄, read⇄, permanent delete).
- **contracts/api.md** — every endpoint, incl. duplicate-returns-existing on POST, bulk "apply to all matching," snapshot capture/serve, archive-org, import/export.
- **contracts/search-grammar.md** — full EBNF + evaluation table + worked examples (`#js promise` = both required; `"AND"` = literal).
- **contracts/netscape-format.md** — field mapping preserving address, title, **tags, and ADD_DATE**; whole-file rejection on malformed input.

### A couple of choices worth your explicit nod

1. **Local server** (vs. a pure browser app) — required for the reasons above. Still single-user, same-device, no accounts.
2. **Tag identity is case-insensitive** — so `News` and `news` are one tag (prevents near-duplicates, matches case-insensitive search). Say if you'd rather tags be case-sensitive.
3. **Favicon + preview images cached locally** on save (best-effort) so the list works offline and survives link rot.

### 👉 At this gate

- **Approve** and I'll run `speckit-tasks` to produce the dependency-ordered task breakdown (I'll bring that back too before implementing).
- **Want changes** to the stack or any design choice? Tell me and I'll revise the plan.

I'll wait for your go-ahead.
